source.title: Exploring the Capabilities of LLMs for Code-Change-Related Tasks
source.authors: Lishui Fan; Jia-Kun Liu; Zhong-Xin Liu; David Lo; Xin Xia; Shan-Ping Li

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some table layouts are flattened or malformed, but the selected results below are legible in the text or tables.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream task performance across model sizes, a different measure and setup from the loss-scaling claim, and reports that larger models do not consistently perform better.
record.gate_note: The paper measures code-change task metrics, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy, power-law fits, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocations. Its size comparisons bear on V6 only. Other model and task results do not test the other listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares two sizes within each LLM family (CodeGen 2B/6B, Llama 2 and Code Llama 7B/13B) on downstream code-change tasks under ICL and LoRA. That is a direct, if narrow, check on V6 (does larger mean better downstream) in a new setting. It does not fit a scaling curve, so T3 fits better than T2. Nothing bears on loss, extrapolation, allocation, shape, other modalities or fit choices.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it should be split by method. Under ICL, larger models do better in Llama 2 and CodeGen but worse in Code Llama, where 7b is best overall. Under LoRA, size differences within a family are not significant. The authors say model family matters more than size; Llama 2 and Code Llama are the best families.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares downstream generation metrics across selected pretrained model sizes and adaptation methods; it does not reproduce a pretraining loss-scaling experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies with model family, task, number of ICL examples, and input format. The paper also reports that example counts and input format affect results.
record.peer_reviewed: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
record.problems: The study uses selected model families and sizes and evaluates downstream code-change metrics rather than pretraining loss. The size comparisons do not fit a scaling curve or establish broad predictability. The paper reports significance testing generally, but no uncertainty estimates for the individual size-comparison values recorded here.
record.rows_left_out: Many other per-model results in Tables 3-7 and 11-15, Appendix Tables 20-21, and category-level results in Table 17 are omitted because they do not add further size-comparison conditions needed to document the reported variation; the paper's broader results on prompts, methods, languages, and code-change categories are outside the tested claim version.

untested.parts: Relation of downstream performance to pretraining loss; predictability, i.e. any fitted trend across more than two sizes. Size ranges are under 3x (2B to 6B, 7B to 13B).
All of it: no pretraining loss is measured.
All of it: fine-tuning is used, but no power-law form is examined.

missing.what: CodeGen-2b vs CodeGen-6b ICL comparisons (6b generally higher, e.g. JITCU GLEU 17.36 vs 2.01 at 7-shot)
LoRA size comparisons: Llama 2-7b vs 13b (CRG 5.74 vs 5.29; JITCU GLEU 63.30 vs 61.81; CMG-Java 12.30 vs 11.73). Code Llama 7b vs 13b is mixed (CRG 4.04 vs 5.61; GLEU 65.23 vs 64.22).
CRG ICL size comparisons, where differences are tiny and mixed within families

record.verdict_notes: The evidence on V6 is narrow: two sizes per family, at most a 3x range. The Code Llama sizes share the same 500B-token code training. The rows come in redundant mirror pairs. Context truncation in ICL (a 1024-token example budget) may interact with model size. The paper cites Kaplan et al. only to explain InCoder's example handling.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power-law fits on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
No pretraining-loss relation or general predictive scaling curve is measured; comparisons cover selected code-change tasks, model families, sizes, and prompting settings.
Fitted scaling exponents, fitting choices, and curvature of loss-scaling curves.

relationships.condition: Code Llama 7B vs 13B, ICL, diff input, CMG and JITCU
relationships.reason: The 13B model scores below the 7B model, e.g. CMG-Java BLEU 4.98 vs 6.19 and JITCU ACC 19.65 vs 23.65 (r1-r8).
relationships.display_finding: The larger model scored lower, including CMG-Java BLEU of 4.98 versus 6.19 and JITCU accuracy of 19.65 versus 23.65.

relationships.condition: Llama 2 7B vs 13B (and, per the text, CodeGen 2B vs 6B), ICL
relationships.reason: The larger model scores higher, e.g. CMG-Java BLEU 5.75 vs 4.16 (r9-r10). The text says larger is better in the Llama 2 and CodeGen families.
relationships.display_finding: Larger variants scored higher in both families, including CMG-Java BLEU of 5.75 versus 4.16.

relationships.condition: LoRA tuning, Llama 2 and Code Llama 7B vs 13B
relationships.reason: Based on the text and Tables 6-7, not on rows: authors call size differences not significant; Llama 2-7b beats 13b on CRG (5.74 vs 5.29), JITCU GLEU and most CMG languages.
relationships.display_finding: Size differences were described as nonsignificant, and Llama 2-7b beat 13b on CRG, 5.74 versus 5.29, as well as JITCU GLEU and most CMG languages.
